definitions.gloss: decluttering; the practice of getting rid of unnecessary possessions
definitions.explanation: a Japanese concept of organizing and simplifying one's life by discarding unneeded items and avoiding accumulation

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しを{機|き}に{断捨離|だんしゃり}した。
{断捨離|だんしゃり}して{部屋|へや}がすっきりした。
examples.english: After decluttering, my room feels refreshed.

examples.japanese: {断捨離|だんしゃり}は{物|もの}を{捨|す}てるだけでなく、{心|こころ}の{整理|せいり}にもつながる。
examples.english: Decluttering isn't just about throwing things away—it also leads to mental clarity.

notes:
FORMS:
{断|だん} (cut off, refuse) + {捨|しゃ} (discard) + {離|り} (detach) → refuse, discard, detach
{断捨離|だんしゃり}する (to declutter)
{断捨離|だんしゃり}を{行|おこな}う (to practice decluttering)

THREE PRINCIPLES:
The term was coined by Hideko Yamashita and is based on yoga philosophy:
- {断|だん}: {断|た}つ (to refuse) - stop buying unnecessary things
- {捨|しゃ}: {捨|す}てる (to discard) - throw away clutter
- {離|り}: {離|はな}れる (to detach) - become free from attachment to things

PHILOSOPHY:
{断捨離|だんしゃり} is more than cleaning—it's a lifestyle philosophy about:
- Living with less
- Mindful consumption
- Mental and physical freedom from possessions

RELATED WORDS:
- ミニマリスト (minimalist)
- {片付|かたづ}け (tidying up)
- {整理整頓|せいりせいとん} (organizing)
